1 Introduction

  • We study the development of the cfMeDIP-seq, a platform used to characterize methylation patterns in cell-free DNA extracted from plasma.

  • The cfMeDIP-seq assay is the result of optimizing the low-input MeDIP-seq protocol of Taiwo et. al. (2012) [1], which in turn was a specialized version of the protocol established by Weber et al. (2005) [2].

  • The sequence data analysis is based on the methods developed for the analysis of data produced under the regular MeDIP-seq protocol (input > 100 ng). See Chavez et al. (2010) [3] and Lienhard et al. 2014 [4] and Lienhard et al. 2017 [5] .

4 Technical Assessments

  1. Proof of concept study - Shen et al. 2018 [7]
    • a superficial dog and pony show with very little verifiable truth

  1. feature selection and modeling - Halla-aho et al. 2022 [8]
    • the lack of reproducibility may be due to the feature selection strategy.

  1. spike-in control normalization - Wilson et al. 2022 [9]
    • spike-in fragments are used for quantification and normalization.
    • there is no verification that the spike-in fragments can assume the role they are asked to fill.

  1. Fragment length distribution - Stutheit-Zhao (2024) [10]
    • ??

  1. Pan-cancer compendium of variability = Zeng et al. 2026 (Nature) [11]
    • a large number of datasets assembled for this analysis allows for an honest assessment of variability, both within and between sites

4.3

  1. spike-in control normalization

  • Wilson et al. 2022 [9]
    • slides
    • Rmarkdown
      • contents of the paper are detailed.
      • Figures
    • Rmarkdown for summary similar to Stutheit-Zhao (2024) - see Section (#frag-len-dist).

  • Additional markdowns
    • framework
    • biological validation
    • NGS_Normalization_Methods_Review

  • Published Data
    • GEO Accession GSE166259:
      • Raw HCT116 cell line data (public)
      • Processed AML patient data (public)
    • EGA Accession EGAS00001005069:
      • Raw AML patient data (controlled access)
      • Available via University Health Network Genomics Data Access Committee
    • Zenodo Deposits:
      • Code for reproducing all analyses: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4683791
      • spiky package: https://doi.org/10.18129/B9.bioc.spiky

  • Wilson et al. 2022 [9] does not use sharp metrics or suitable evaluation data to assess the success of the normalization procedure.
    • For model performance, Used held-out spike-ins to assess prediction accuracy
      • this tells us nothing about the relevant performance - are the sample normalized methylation profiles better than the un-normalized methylation profiles.
      • the usefulness of the normalization step can only be judged by examining the normalized methylation profiles of samples with some designed or known truth.


  • As a normalization method the spike-in control normalization remains unproven.


4.4

  1. Fragment length distribution
  • Stutheit-Zhao (2024) [10] show that the distribution of fragment lengths adds information to sequence data when trying to discriminate between cancer and non-cancer samples.
    • Rmarkdown
    • This article contributes more examples of innovative analyses that are not vetted to any reasonable degree. There are three methodologies introduced:
      • 1- Methylation Probability Estimation to get a Cancer-Specific Methylation (CSM) Score
        • fitting a model with an unmethylated component to a data set which only targets methylated DNA fragments is an interesting approach.
        • How does it work? Why does it work? We are provided no clue.
      • 2- Using reference distribution of fragment length for normal and cancer populations to obtain a Fragment length score.
        • Using fragment lengths from samples processed on a different platform is another interesting choice.
      • 3- The two scores are combined with the weighting determined by a logistic regression fit the linear combination of both.
        • the assumption of independent additive effects should be checked.
knitr::include_graphics( "fragment_length/Figure2B.png", dpi=50)

Figure 2B from Stutheit-Zhao (2024). The figure indicates that this fragment length feature adds very little predictive power, if any, to the methylation index. Recall that this fragment length feature is computed using a reference distribution of fragment length collected using a different platform.



  • The analyses have apparent flaws so one should not generalize these results too broadly, if al all.
    • Fragmentation patterns in cfDNA have proven to be informative in detecting the presence of cancer in many contexts. Using a bad reference may be he problem here.
    • To Do: a literature review on the ways fragmentation patterns can be recorded.
